One folder.One brand.

A 32-second reel about keeping a brand the same in every AI-made video. Ask AI for ten ads and you get ten different brands; write the brand into one folder that Claude reads before every video, and every correction becomes a rule. Everything on screen is drawn in code on an HTML canvas, timed to the voice word by word. Below: how the reel was made, and the folder itself, ready to copy.

01 · The idea

Ten ads, ten brands.

Ask an AI for ten ads with no rules and every one comes back in a different colour, font and tone. The fix isn't a better prompt each time; it's a place where the brand lives, that the AI reads before it starts. Big brands always had one: a printed manual. Ours is a folder, and it learns.

So the reel opens on the problem (ten clashing ads for one can of sparkling water), turns the folder into the hero, shows what goes inside it and how a correction becomes a rule, and closes by putting an old printed manual next to the folder: the same ten ads, now all on brand.

02 · The folder

How we set one up.

This is the setup from the reel. One folder per brand, inside your project. Claude reads it before every video, and it grows every time you correct something.

folder structure
brand/
  brand.md        <- the rules Claude reads first
  logo/           <- logo files (SVG, or PNG with transparency)
  fonts/          <- the brand's font files
  refs/           <- 3-5 videos or posts the brand loves
  never/          <- examples of what the brand never wants
brand/brand.md · template
# Brand: [name]
Read this whole file before writing any script, scene or caption.

## Look
- Colours: [primary #hex] · [secondary #hex] · [accent #hex, only on the focus]
- Type: [headline font] for titles, [body font] for text. Never more than two.
- Logo: brand/logo/[file]. Visible at least once every ~6 seconds, inside the safe zone.

## Pace
- One idea per block of ~3 s. No text on screen for less than 1.5 s.
- Cut every [1.5-2.5] s. Camera moves are slow pushes, never shakes.

## Voice
- [3 words for the tone]. Example line: "[a sentence the brand would say]".

## Never
- [e.g. neon, stock "SALE!!!" bursts, more than one exclamation mark]
- [e.g. words the brand never uses]

## Rules (added from corrections, newest first)
- [date] rule 01: [the correction, written as a rule]

Keep it short. A page Claude can read in one go beats a 200-page manual. Hex codes, font names and numbers ("cut every 1.8 s") work better than adjectives ("clean", "modern").

CLAUDE.md · add these lines to your project
Before making any video, read brand/brand.md and look at brand/refs/ and brand/never/.
Follow every rule in brand.md. If a request conflicts with a rule, tell me before you build.
When I correct something in a draft, turn the correction into a new line under "Rules" in brand.md,
with today's date, written so it applies to future videos and not only to this one.
Never edit or delete an existing rule without asking me first.
Step 01

Fill the folder.

Colours as hex, the font files, the logo, 3–5 references the brand loves and a few examples of what it never wants. The "never" list is the part most people skip, and the one that saves the most corrections.

Step 02

Make the first reel.

Ask Claude to read brand.md first and say which rules apply before it builds. Review a stills sheet before any render.

Step 03

Correct once, as a rule.

When something is off, say it once and ask for it to become a rule. The next reel starts with it already in the folder.

first prompt · claude code
Make a 30-second vertical reel (1080x1920, 30 fps) for the brand in brand/.
Read brand/brand.md first and tell me in 3 lines which rules apply to this reel.
Then write the script, show me a stills sheet (one frame every 1.5 s) before rendering,
and only render the final after I approve it.
a correction that becomes a rule · claude code
Correction: the logo is too small in every frame.
Fix it in this reel, then add it to brand.md as a rule so the next reels already know.
03 · References

Style from one reel, story from ours.

The look was studied frame by frame from an editorial brand-launch reel, for its style only: warm paper, ink lines that draw themselves, a serif with one italic word, a low-poly mesh as the transition and a small glowing dot that leads the eye. Its brand, story and text were not used.

An invented brand

Mareta, a grapefruit sparkling water, drawn entirely in code: a coral can, a teal serif wordmark, a half-grapefruit mark. Ten off-brand versions for the hook, the true one for everything after.

One conductor

The orange Claude spark carries the eye through the whole reel: it sends the prompt, lands on the folder, reads brand.md line by line and rides the corrected reel out.

A colour per block

Cream, navy, cream, amber, deep green, clay, cream. Light and dark alternate, so every new idea starts on a new background.

#F6F0E6 cream#141A2E navy#F2C14E amber#1F4D3A green#D97757 clay
A presenter that moves around

Catalina, from her real images only, stands in a different place in each block: left when she points at the content, right when she thinks or points at you, centre for the wink at the end. She steps out for the payoff.

04 · Claude session

One kit, then three builders.

00:01 · master prompt · claude code
Make a 32-second vertical edu reel for The AI Editing Lab, 1080x1920 at 30 fps, all in English. Topic: keeping a brand the same in every AI-made video with one folder Claude reads.

1. Script (use it word for word): "Ask AI for ten ads for your brand and you'll get ten different brands. There's one folder that fixes that, and the one reading it isn't a person. At The AI Editing Lab, we write your brand into it, and Claude reads it before every video. Your colors, your fonts, how fast you cut, even what you never want to see. When you correct something, that note becomes a new rule, so the next reel already knows. Every brand used to have a manual. Now yours edits your videos. Comment MANUAL and I'll send you how we set one up."

2. Voice. ElevenLabs, voice "Jessica", natural speed (1.0), with every word's start and end saved; every cue reads a word time.

3. Brand. Invent one: Mareta, grapefruit sparkling water in a coral can, teal lowercase serif wordmark. Draw ten off-brand versions of its ad (neon, chrome, comic, corporate...) and the true one.

4. Look. Warm paper, ink lines that draw themselves, a serif with one italic word, a low-poly triangle mesh as the transition, an orange Claude spark that leads the eye. One background colour per block, alternating light and dark.

5. Story. Chaos first (ten clashing ads), then the folder, what goes in it, a correction that becomes a rule, an old printed manual next to the folder, and the same ten ads now on brand.

6. Layout. Leave a rectangle empty in each block for our presenter (left, right or centre; I'll give you the table). Nothing important below y 1400.

7. Process. Build a shared kit and the first two blocks, show me the stills, then build the rest in parallel. Run the motion and originality checks before the final render.

What came back: a block-by-block storyboard, the narration with 100 time-stamped words, a shared kit (the folder that draws itself, the spark, the mesh wipe, the Mareta ads) and the first two blocks. Then three builders made the other five blocks at the same time from the same kit and word clock.

00:02 · stills before render · claude code
Before the final render, export a stills sheet: one frame every 1.5 seconds from frame 0, with the presenter composited and the safe-zone guide in red. Check that every block is full at its cut, the presenter never covers content, and the text reads on a phone. Fix everything in one pass.

What came back: 32.1 seconds at 1080×1920 and 30 fps, 14 Mbps, the voice plus 55 sound effects on real events, mixed at −14.5 LUFS.

06 · Decisions

Where the taste is.

01

Start with the problem

The first idea was a history hook about a famous printed manual. We cut it: it spent five seconds on someone else's logo before saying what the Lab does.

02

A brand that doesn't exist

An invented brand can be shown wrong ten times without hurting anyone, and drawn in code from the can to the wordmark.

03

The same wall, in order

The payoff reuses the exact 5×2 wall from the hook, so the change reads without a word.

04

Every cue is a word

The folder draws on "folder", the stamp lands on "Lab", the X on "never", the paper plane becomes a rule on "rule".
